title: Cricket Is Going to the Olympics. India Women Are Already In.
excerpt: The IOC and ICC have unveiled the qualification pathway for LA 2028 — cricket's first Olympic appearance in 128 years. India's women qualified through the T20 World Cup. The men need to hold their ranking.
body:
India's women cricketers have done something that no Indian cricket team has done in the sport's 148-year organized history: qualified for the Olympic Games.

The International Cricket Council and the International Olympic Committee jointly confirmed on Monday that the qualification pathway for LA 2028 is set. Cricket will return to the Olympics for the first time since the 1900 Paris Games — a gap of 128 years — and India's women are among the first four nations to book their tickets.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaLImKaEila/

## How They Got In

The women's qualification pathway uses the ongoing T20 World Cup in England as the primary qualifying event. The highest-placed eligible team from each of four continents — Asia, Oceania, Europe, and Africa — earns a direct Olympic berth.

India, despite being knocked out of the tournament by Australia on Sunday at Lord's, finished as Asia's best-performing team. Australia qualified for Oceania, Great Britain (through England) for Europe, and South Africa for Africa. That is four of the six spots filled.

The remaining two berths will be decided differently. The United States, as hosts, receive an automatic place — but only if they appear in the ICC's top 15 T20I rankings at some point between June 30, 2026, and December 31, 2026. The sixth and final spot will be decided through a new ICC Olympics Qualifier tournament in 2027.

## The Men's Path Is Different — and More Precarious



> **"Jay Shah, the ICC chair, called it a "landmark moment" for the sport."**


India's men are heavy favourites to qualify, but their path is not yet sealed. Unlike the women's event, the men's qualification relies on ICC T20I rankings as of December 31, 2026. The four highest-ranked eligible teams from four different continents — Asia, Africa, Europe, and Oceania — will qualify directly.

India, as the reigning T20 World Cup champions and the top-ranked men's T20I side in Asia, are near-certain to qualify. But the rankings cut-off is six months away. Pakistan, ranked close behind, would need to overtake India to steal Asia's automatic spot — an unlikely but mathematically possible scenario.

The current picture for the men's event looks like this: India from Asia, Great Britain (through England's ranking) from Europe, South Africa from Africa, and Australia from Oceania. The USA get a host berth on the same conditions as the women's event. The final spot goes through the qualifier.


![International Olympic Committee — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Si%C3%A8ge_CIO_2020_%281%29.jpg/3840px-Si%C3%A8ge_CIO_2020_%281%29.jpg)


## The West Indies Problem

One of the most intriguing wrinkles in the pathway involves the West Indies. As a composite ICC member representing multiple Caribbean nations, the West Indies are not recognized as an IOC National Olympic Committee — meaning they cannot compete in the Olympics as a single team.

If either the men's or women's West Indies teams finish among the eight highest-ranked non-qualified sides, a dedicated Caribbean Qualifier will determine which individual nation represents the region at the ICC Olympics Qualifier. It is a significant structural challenge for one of cricket's most decorated sides.

## What LA Means for the Diaspora

The venue could not be more fitting. Cricket at LA 2028 will be played at the Fairgrounds Stadium in Pomona, roughly 50 kilometres east of downtown Los Angeles — in the heart of one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the world.

Southern California is home to hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans, and the prospect of watching Harmanpreet Kaur, Smriti Mandhana, and Jasprit Bumrah compete for Olympic gold on American soil is something that would have been unimaginable even five years ago. The Games will feature six teams each in the men's and women's T20 tournaments, with squads of up to 15 players. A total of 180 athletes — 90 men and 90 women — will take part.

Jay Shah, the ICC chair, called it a "landmark moment" for the sport. "This is an historic moment, and one of great opportunity for our Members, as we continue to grow the game and take it to new audiences around the world," Shah said.

## The Bigger Picture

For Indian cricket, the Olympics represent a frontier that even the IPL and the World Cup never fully opened. The Olympics carry a different weight — they reach audiences that do not follow cricket, they command global media attention that dwarfs any bilateral series, and they place cricket alongside athletics, swimming, and gymnastics on the biggest sporting stage on earth.

The Indian women's team may have exited the T20 World Cup at Lord's, but their performances in England were enough to write them into history. Harmanpreet Kaur, who at 37 became the oldest Indian to score a T20 World Cup half-century, and Deepti Sharma, who broke the all-time wicket-taking record during the tournament, will be at the centre of India's Olympic preparations.

For the men, the next six months of T20I rankings will matter more than any single series. India's five-match T20I tour of England, starting July 1, will be the first meaningful data point. Every match, every ranking point, now carries Olympic weight.

Cricket in the Olympics is no longer a dream. For India's women, it is a date: July 12, 2028, in Los Angeles.
